newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico 1997 social spending 277 bln pesos -Zedillo.
newsitem.headline: Mexico 1997 social spending 277 bln pesos -Zedillo.

text.p: The Mexican government has earmarked 277.4 billion pesos for social spending in 1997, 9.3 percent more than in 1996, in order to bolster development in highly marginalized areas, President Ernesto Zedillo said Monday.
"Federal social spending in 1997 will be 277.420 billion pesos. This figure represents the highest proportion of budget spending in the last 10 years," Zedillo told government officials.
Zedillo, speaking at a ceremony to unveil the Social Development Ministry's 1997 program, said the figure was equivalent to nine percent of gross domestic product estimated for 1997.
"This figure also means we will spend 56 centavos out of every peso in the federal budget on social spending," Zedillo said.
